text.p: Austria gave their World Cup qualification chances a boost on Wednesday when an 11th-minute goal from Andreas Herzog proved enough to secure victory over a sluggish-looking Sweden.
Austria, who shared a goalless draw with Scotland in August, looked composed and confident against group four leaders Sweden, unable to unleash their Italian-based attacking formation.
The previously formidable combination of Kennet Andersson of Bologna and Roma's Martin Dahlin lacked sparkle and Andersson left the field injured after missing a penalty in the 30th minute.
Austria were content to rest on their laurels in the second half, defending desperately at times against a ragged-looking Swedish attack who squandered several good chances to equalise.
In a scrappy, niggly match, Czech referee Vaclav Krondl used his yellow card five times, booking three Austrians.

The Austrian defence appeared nervous in the opening minutes but, against the run of play, Werder Bremen striker Herzog quickly capitalised on a disastrous mistake by Swedish defender Patrik Andersson.

Andersson fluffed his 11th minute clearance on the edge of the Swedish penalty box and Herzog gratefully accepted the ball, dribbling into the area and lashing the ball left-footed past Thomas Ravelli, making his 132nd appearance for Sweden.
Austria then piled on the pressure before Sweden were awarded a somewhat lucky penalty when Markus Schopp was adjudged to have tripped Swedish attacker Jesper Blomqvist.
Kennet Andersson, appearing in bright yellow boots, was guilty of a feeble kick which hardly tested goalkeeper Michael Konsel.
Sweden were unable to penetrate the Austrian defence in the second half, although Dahlin came close twice and Par Zetterberg, the pick of Sweden's team saw a fierce volley deflected just wide.

Sweden: 1-Thomas Ravelli; 2-Roland Nilsson, 3-Patrik Andersson, 4-Joachim Bjorklund, 5-Jesper Blomqvist, 6-Stefan Schwarz, 7-Par Zetterberg, 8-Klas Ingesson (16-Hakan Mild), 67th): 9-Jonas Thern, 10-Martin Dahlin (18-Andreas Andersson, 83rd), 11-Kennet Andersson (17-Henrik Larsson, 42nd).

Austria: 1-Michael Konsel; 2-Markus Schopp (16-Michael Hatz, 77th), 3-Peter Schottel, 4-Anton Pfeffer, 5-Wolfgang Feiersinger: 6-Andreas Heraf, 7-Adolf Hutter, 8-Arnold Wetl: 9-Anton Polster, 10-Andreas Herzog, 11-Peter Stoger (18-Dieter Ramusch, 71st).
